findings.title: A backup code alone logs in without a password when any totpCode is sent too
findings.body: The password is checked only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever `backupCode` is set, and it never looks at `totpCode`. So a request to the credentials provider with `{ email, password: "", totpCode: "x", backupCode: <valid code> }` skips the password check, also gets past lines 113 and 117 for a CAL user who has a password, and then succeeds on the backup code. A leaked backup code is a static secret that often sits in the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`, and it becomes enough to take over the account on its own. Before this change, the totpCode-skips-password path still needed a valid TOTP from the user's device. Fix: verify the password inside the backup-code branch, or make the line 121 condition `user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode)`. You could also reject requests that carry both `totpCode` and `backupCode`.

findings.title: Closing the backup-codes step with Escape or an overlay click leaves the settings page saying 2FA is off
findings.body: After a successful enable, `handleEnable` now moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135) instead of calling `onEnable()`. Only the Close button (lines 266-270) calls `onEnable`, which in turn calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:65-67). If the dialog is dismissed through `onOpenChange` (Escape or a click outside), the parent only toggles `enableModalOpen` (two-factor-auth.tsx:64). The server already has `twoFactorEnabled: true`, but `me` is never refetched, so the switch still shows 2FA as disabled and nothing tells the user. `resetState()` is skipped as well, so the modal reopens on the backup-codes step. Fix: handle dismissal in this step by calling `onEnable`/`resetState` from the `onOpenChange` path, or block outside-dismiss while this step is shown.

findings.title: Using up a backup code is read-modify-write, so the same code can work twice
findings.body: The codes are read with the user (line 89), changed in memory, and written back without any condition (lines 149-156). Two logins running at the same time with the same code both find it at `indexOf` and both succeed, which breaks the promise in the locale text that each code works "exactly once". The per-email rate limit narrows the window but does not close it. An `updateMany` that matches the previous `backupCodes` ciphertext, plus a check on the affected row count, would make the step atomic.

findings.title: `missing_backup_codes` points locked-out users to a settings page they cannot reach
findings.body: This message appears on the login page (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:158) for users who turned on 2FA before this feature existed. They have no backup codes, and by definition they cannot log in to reach settings. Even in settings there is no way to generate codes except disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Consider saying that no backup codes exist for the account and pointing to support, or to the TOTP/disable-and-re-enable path.

findings.title: The default export of BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`
findings.body: The component is copied from TwoFactor.tsx and keeps the name `TwoFactor`. In React DevTools and stack traces it then looks the same as the real `TwoFactor` component, which both login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal render next to it. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

contracts.action: Login with a backup code through the credentials provider
contracts.equivalent_path: TOTP branch of the same authorize function (lines 157-186)
contracts.before_after: Both run after the rate limit (109-111) and after the password check, which runs only when totpCode is absent (121-129). The backup branch does not check for totpCode, so the password step can be skipped by also sending a totpCode. On success it nulls the matched code and re-encrypts the list.
contracts.visible_effect: On success, signIn returns no error and login.tsx:155 routes to callbackUrl. IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes map to locale messages at login.tsx:157-158.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing key throws InternalServerError. A corrupt ciphertext makes JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt throw, which shows the generic error. The update is not atomic, so concurrent reuse can succeed.

contracts.action: Show backup codes after enabling 2FA instead of calling onEnable
contracts.equivalent_path: The old flow called onEnable() right after enable succeeded, which invalidated viewer.me
contracts.before_after: onEnable/resetState now run only from the Close button. Dismissing through onOpenChange only toggles the parent's open state.
contracts.visible_effect: The settings switch updates only after Close. On Escape or an overlay click it stays off even though 2FA is enabled on the server.
contracts.failure_mode: The UI state is wrong with no message, and the modal reopens on the backup-codes step.

contracts.action: Download button wrapped in an anchor inside the enable Form
contracts.equivalent_path: Copy and Close buttons in the same footer
contracts.before_after: Button defaults to type="button", so clicking Download does not submit the form, and the anchor's default download action goes ahead using the object URL created in handleSetup.
contracts.visible_effect: The browser downloads cal-backup-codes.txt. The e2e test asserts the filename.

contracts.equivalent_path: TOTP branch in the same handler (69-100)
contracts.before_after: For CAL users the password is verified first (40-45). The backup code is matched and then all codes are cleared along with the secret (102-111).
contracts.visible_effect: On a 200 the modal resets and calls onDisable, which invalidates me. Errors map to locale strings in DisableTwoFactorModal.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing key throws, which returns a 500 and shows the something_went_wrong message.

summary: This PR adds 2FA backup codes: they are generated at setup, shown and downloadable after enabling, and accepted at login and when disabling 2FA. One blocker: the credentials provider checks the password only when no `totpCode` is sent, and the new backup-code branch does not check for `totpCode`. A request with a dummy `totpCode` and a valid backup code therefore logs in without a password. One fix: dismissing the new backup-codes step with Escape or an overlay click never calls `onEnable`, so the settings switch shows 2FA as off while it is on. Smaller points: the code is consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write, the `missing_backup_codes` message is misleading, and the `BackupCode` component is exported under the name `TwoFactor`.
